A client may request cancellation of a project before completion.

The financial consequences of cancellation should depend on the project agreement, the amount of work already completed, and any agreed deposit or cancellation terms.

A creator may request cancellation when circumstances prevent the creator from reasonably completing the project.

The creator should communicate the situation to the client as soon as reasonably possible.
When a project is cancelled, the parties should account for work already completed and any non-refundable costs that were agreed upon before the project began.

Any refund should be determined according to the agreed cancellation terms.

If the project agreement does not clearly address cancellation, the parties should attempt to reach a reasonable agreement based on work completed and payments already made.

The expected delivery date should be agreed upon before the project begins.

Delivery estimates may change when the client requests additional work, provides required information late, or changes the original scope.

The client is responsible for providing information, assets, approvals, and other materials required for the creator to complete the project.

Delays in receiving required materials may affect the delivery date.

Final deliverables should be provided according to the format and delivery method agreed upon by the parties.

The creator should confirm that the client has received the final deliverables when practical.

If the creator expects a significant delay, the creator should inform the client and provide an updated estimated delivery date.

The parties may agree to modify the project schedule when circumstances outside the original plan affect delivery.

The client should review delivered work within the review period specified in the project agreement.

Acceptance requirements should be agreed upon before work begins when the project requires formal approval.

The client and creator should agree on the project price, currency, payment schedule, and payment method before work begins.

The agreed payment terms should be recorded in the project agreement.

A project may require an upfront deposit before work begins.

The deposit amount and whether it is refundable should be clearly agreed upon before the project starts.

Creators may pause delivery of unfinished work when an agreed payment is overdue, subject to the terms of the project agreement.

The creator should communicate the outstanding amount and payment status to the client before pausing work.

Work outside the agreed project scope may require an additional fee.

The creator should confirm the additional cost with the client before beginning substantial additional work.

Refund eligibility depends on the agreed project terms and the amount of work already completed.

Any refund policy should be communicated clearly before the project begins.

CreatorFlow provides tools that help creators and clients organize creative projects, prepare business terms, analyze project requirements, and generate draft documents.

CreatorFlow generated documents are provided as reference material and should be reviewed by the relevant parties before use.

Users are responsible for providing accurate project information and reviewing generated documents before relying on them.

Users should not use CreatorFlow to intentionally provide misleading, fraudulent, or unlawful information.

AI-generated content may contain errors or omissions. Users are responsible for reviewing generated content and determining whether it is appropriate for their specific situation.

CreatorFlow does not guarantee that generated business or legal language is complete, accurate, or suitable for every jurisdiction.

Ownership of project deliverables should be determined by the agreement between the relevant parties.

Unless otherwise agreed, creators retain ownership of their pre-existing materials, tools, templates, and intellectual property used to produce a project.
Users should avoid submitting confidential information unless they are comfortable with the way the relevant service processes that information.
Users should attempt to resolve project disputes through direct communication and reference the applicable project agreement before escalating a dispute.
CreatorFlow is a software tool and does not provide legal advice. Generated terms and policies are reference drafts and should be reviewed by a qualified professional when appropriate.

Each standard project includes up to two rounds of revisions.

A revision round means one consolidated set of requested changes submitted by the client after receiving a draft.

Requests beyond the included revision rounds may require an additional fee.

The creator should confirm the additional fee with the client before beginning additional revision work.

A request that substantially changes the original project requirements may be treated as additional work rather than a normal revision.

The creator should discuss the change in scope and any additional fee with the client before proceeding.

Clients should provide revision requests within the review period specified in the project agreement.

If no review period has been agreed, the parties should establish a reasonable review period before work begins.
